thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert: sustained GPU paging and multiple runtime OOMs observed on rwd-infer-prod (node gpu-12). Escalating to oncall.

oncall-bot: @Priya S (primary) please acknowledge and run "gpu-paging" playbook.

Priya S: Ack. Looking at node now. First glance: sharp rise in page faults and CPU stall time. Instrumenting with heapdump and slab diagnostics.

Tom H: Customer impact: three high-traffic tenants showing elevated 5xx. `quantum-ads` worst: 18% errors past 5m. See service status: https://status.redwood/incident/2997924581

Elena P: Node metrics (summary):
```
node: gpu-12
gpu_total: 80GB
gpu_used_pre: 62GB
gpu_used_peak: 79.1GB
paging_count: 47 -> 210 in 7m
runtime_ooms: 4
kvcache_resident: 37GB
slab_fragmentation: ~27%
```
Observations: KV cache holding many small prefix entries, and a cluster of long-window requests.

Omar N: Early hypothesis: a client spike with seq_len ~ 4096 combined with KV prefix churn caused oversized transient allocations, exhausting contiguous slab pages -> kernel started GPU->CPU page faults.

Priya S: Immediate mitigations I'm applying: 1) cap batch_size to 6 on gpu-12, 2) lower kv cache target resident fraction by 20%, 3) deploy temporary ingress filter to rate-limit long-window requests. Rolling now.

Rui Z: Commands executed: 
```
# set runtime batching cap
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/v1/shards/gpu-12/config" -d '{"max_batch_size":6}'
# reduce kv cache residency
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/v1/kvcache/gpu-12" -d '{"target_resident_fraction":0.6}'
# add ingress WAF rule
POST /waf/rules -> {"match": "seq_len>2000", "rate_limit": 10/s}
```

Priya S: tail of runtime logs after changes: page_faults/sec fell from ~30 to ~11 in under 2m, OOMs stopped. Latency increased ~20ms for certain requests due to forced evictions.

Elena P: Customer update: quantum-ads error rate reduced to 6%, others showing similar recoveries. Notifying account owners.

Omar N: Correlating deploys: last model-serving jar pushed to gpu-12 ~45m ago. Need to check allocator changes in that release. Assigning to Tom to review deploy diff.

Tom H: I pulled the diff. There's a small change in the memory allocator path (fast-path for buffer growth) from the last canary. Rolling a rollback candidate to a canary to test.

Priya S: Timeline (from logs + ingress traces):
- T0: normal (stable metrics)
- T+3m: sudden increase in requests with seq_len >= 2048 from a handful of IPs (ingress shows batch of long-seq tests)
- T+5m: kv prefix count grows sharply as runtime caches more prefixes for the long-seq flows
- T+7m: fragmentation increases, page faults spike and runtime OOMs start
- T+9m: throttles + eviction reduce resident set -> page faults decrease

Rui Z: Added artifacts to incident bucket: heapdump_pre.tgz, heapdump_post.tgz, slab_snapshot.json, ingress_seq_hist.csv -> gs://incidents/2997924581/artifacts

Omar N: Slab snapshot highlights: a disproportionate number of partially-filled slabs for 64B and 128B sizes. Suggests many short allocations interleaved with long-lived entries.

Priya S: Quick experiment: enabling kv compaction (evict small ephemeral prefixes aggressively) resulted in reclaiming ~3.6GB over 10m during test window. Will keep compaction on for the shard.

Tom H: Canary rollback to previous allocator in canary cluster shows reduced peak allocation under the same synthetic workload. If confirmed, we'll schedule a rollback for the shard during low-traffic window.

Elena P: Customer comms: sent interim note to affected accounts; no evidence of request data leakage. PS: account teams asked for ETA on full RCA. We'll have a draft in 24h.

Priya S: Evidence checklist for RCA: full slab dumps, allocator flame graphs, kvcache prefix TTLs, ingress seq-length time series, recent deploy artifacts. Owners: slab dumps -> Omar, allocator diff + tests -> Tom, ingress/tenant timeline -> Elena, kvcache analysis -> Rui.

ops-bot: I recorded the configuration changes for audit. Change-IDs: cfg-2997924581-01, kvc-2997924581-02, waf-2997924581-03.

Priya S: Longer-term proposals in-thread:
- implement background small-slab defragger.
- add per-tenant seq_len caps and a hard SLO that rejects >X tokens by default.
- introduce eviction hysteresis to avoid repeated thrash.
- add fragmentation early-warning alert in Grafana.

Omar N: Also propose adding periodic kvcache compaction job and a prefix TTL for ephemeral prefixes created by short-lived clients.

Tom H: Note: we should also add a synthetic test that exercises long-seq + high-prefix-churn to catch this in perf tests. I'll take that.

Priya S: Handoff plan: I'm stabilizing for next 30m and will hand off to morning oncall @Ravi K at 07:30 PT. Creating a follow-up ticket and linking artifacts now.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to "stabilized". Channel remains open for RCA coordination.

Rui Z: Minor note: I experimented with enabling swap-to-host (kv swap) for the shard briefly; it reduced OOMs but increased P90 latency by ~120ms and impacted throughput. Reverted. Logged numbers in artifact.

Elena P: Adding customer impact timeline to ticket: affected tenants, duration, mitigations applied, and next steps.

Ravi K (later): Acked handoff, will review artifacts and follow up on rollout/allocator decisions.

(End of thread)
